Recovery · Latvia

Foreign UAV wreckage found in Latvia’s Liepna parish

24 October 2026 · Liepna · foreign UAV discovery

Confirmed foreign UAV discovery; origin unresolved

Latvian armed forces confirmed the discovery of a foreign UAV in Liepna parish on 24 October. Police verified wreckage in forest; no civilian injuries, infrastructure damage or continuing danger were reported.

Authorities said it may have entered Latvian airspace on 18 October. The record uses the confirmed discovery date, not an assumed crash date. National origin, operator, route and intent remain unknown.

A ministerial suggestion that a Ukrainian drone might have been damaged over Russia and glided into Latvia is explicitly conditional; it does not establish origin or route.

Attribution and uncertainty

Origin / operator / attribution
NBS identified a foreign UAV; national origin, operator and intent unknown.
Investigation / uncertainty
Discovery is confirmed; the proposed 18 October arrival date remains uncertain. In the LSM report, minister Raivis Melnis conditionally suggested that IF Ukrainian, the drone might have been hit over Russia and glided into Latvia. This is a hypothesis, not established nationality, route or cause.

Date basis
Discovery confirmed on 24 October. NBS said possible airspace entry was on 18 October; entry and crash times remain unconfirmed.

Forest in Liepna parish, Alūksne municipality, Latvia; EU land. Exact site unpublished.
Event categories
Foreign UAV discovery; recovery
What was reported
Police confirmed reported wreckage in difficult-access forest on 24 October. Earlier searches followed an explosion-like noise but had ended without confirmation.
Aircraft / vessel / quantity
One foreign UAV; model unspecified.
Origin / operator / attribution
NBS identified a foreign UAV; national origin, operator and intent unknown.
Damage / casualties / disruption
NBS reported no civilian injuries, civilian infrastructure damage or continuing threat.
Response / outcome
Police opened a criminal investigation and completed site work on 24 October. NBS explosive-ordnance specialists collected the wreckage; NBS also opened an internal review of the incident response.
Investigation / uncertainty
Discovery is confirmed; the proposed 18 October arrival date remains uncertain. In the LSM report, minister Raivis Melnis conditionally suggested that IF Ukrainian, the drone might have been hit over Russia and glided into Latvia. This is a hypothesis, not established nationality, route or cause.
Route / entry mechanism
Unknown; possible entry into Latvian airspace on 18 October according to NBS.
Explosive payload
Not established in the reviewed official account.
Counting / links
Separate Latvian recovery, not the Juodžionys Lithuanian crash N096. No evidence establishes a link between the aircraft.
